solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, answers clash); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One was bound to land to the sound of waves breaking

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word that is said the same as the one the following words supply

parts.note: breaking waves on a shore are surf

explanation.surface: Someone is lulled ashore by the noise of breakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One was bound to land' reads like a sailor longing for shore; it means a feudal labourer tied to an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval serf was legally tied to the estate of the lord and could not leave it.

clue.text: One conceals the point of security

definitions.text: One conceals the point of security

parts.words: One conceals the point of security
parts.note: read literally: a fastener whose sharp tip is hidden in a clasp, the clasp making it safe to use

explanation.surface: A spy hides the main purpose of a security operation.
explanation.definitionFit: This fastener has a guard that covers its sharp end, so the point is concealed for safety.

clue.text: Uniformed host in troubled time

indicators.note: troubled suggests stirred up and disturbed, so the letters before it are mixed

explanation.surface: A host in uniform is having a difficult time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges UNIFORMED HOST IN, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists treat time as a further dimension beyond length, breadth and height.

clue.text: Felt a rapport with him at speed bumps

indicators.note: bumps suggests knocking things out of place, so these letters are jolted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sympathised with a man driving fast over speed bumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumps' is a verb meaning jolts, rearranging HIM AT SPEED; 'speed bumps' is a false phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To empathise is to share and understand the feelings of another person.

clue.text: Fear the nursery is full of clay

indicators.note: the words before it are said to contain something, so the answer is concealed within their letters

explanation.surface: A child dreads that the playroom is messy with modelling clay.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across fEAR THE Nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen pots are made of baked clay or earth.

clue.text: Soft fruit, mature, is down

parts.note: a plum is a soft stone fruit
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A ripe plum has fallen to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like 'fallen', but it means soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is the soft fine feathering of a bird, part of its whole feather coat.

clue.text: A couple of favourites up for a dance

parts.note: a couple means two

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: pets are favourites, as a teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Two favourite people get up to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-step is a ballroom dance in march or polka time.

clue.text: Unusual line on nice squat of little importance

indicators.note: unusual signals that the following words appear in an odd, rearranged form

explanation.surface: An odd line drawn on a pleasant squat building matters little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges LINE ON NICE SQUAT, fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inconsequential has no significant result, so it is trivial.

clue.text: Initially doubt urge to discard

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: an itch is an urge, as an itch to travel

explanation.surface: Doubts first prompt a desire to throw something away.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is informally to get rid of it.

clue.text: Frills made from pieces of four by two

indicators.note: by two says the rearranged word is taken twice over
breaking a word into pieces lets the letters be reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Decorative trim is cut from four-by-two timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces of' rearranges FOUR into FROU; 'by two' doubles it. 'Four by two' is a standard timber size, which disguises this.
explanation.definitionFit: Frou-frou means fussy ornamentation such as frills on clothing.

clue.text: Officer in charge of sect dealing in the supernatural

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding, the officer in charge
a sect is a cult

explanation.surface: The head of a religious group is dabbling in magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Occult arts concern hidden magical or supernatural powers.

clue.text: Which church has a natural roof covering?

parts.note: that and which are interchangeable relative pronouns

explanation.surface: A question asks which church has a roof made from natural materials.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw or reeds laid on a roof form a covering made from plant material.

clue.text: Cause amazement with regard to backing wrong hotel

parts.note: as to means with regard to

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for wrong is read from its end

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: People are shocked at someone supporting a bad hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support for the hotel, but signals a reversal, giving NIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone is to amaze or astound them.

clue.text: Sun exclusive — almost!

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: sole means exclusive, as in sole rights

explanation.surface: A newspaper nearly has an exclusive story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' looks like the British tabloid, fitting 'exclusive', but it is the Latin name for the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sol is the Latin name for the sun, used in astronomy and poetry.

clue.text: Coppers covering game beginning to display wisdom

indicators.note: covering says the coins word wraps around what follows

parts.note: pence are copper coins, so coppers
RU is rugby union, the game

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Police officers covering a match start to show good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police officers, but means copper coins; 'covering' wraps them round the game and the first letter of display.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is careful good judgement, close to wisdom.

clue.text: Dish bound to be rejected with clam inside

indicators.note: rejected suggests thrown back, so the word for bound is read backwards

parts.note: a bound is a leap

indicators.note: inside asks for the inner letters of the word, its first and last removed

explanation.surface: A seafood dish is sure to be sent back because of a clam within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to be' reads as 'certain to be', but 'bound' is a jump, and 'to be rejected' turns it into PAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Spanish rice dish, often made with seafood.

clue.text: Teacher promoting a mother's capital

indicators.note: promoting means raising up; in a down clue the letter a moves higher, nearer the start

parts.note: a master is a schoolteacher
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A teacher is advancing his mother's interests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting a' moves the A of MASTER up to give AMSTER; 'mother' is DAM, the word for an animal's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the capital city of the Netherlands.

clue.text: New exam to include end of term average

indicators.note: to include says the exam word takes in the next letter

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A new test with an end-of-term section is ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal means usual or typical, which is what an average is.

clue.text: Eggs on veal regularly dropped

indicators.note: regularly dropped says every other letter is lost, leaving alternate letters

explanation.surface: Eggs placed on veal are often left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking letters 1, 3 and 5 of ONVEAL gives O, V, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the Latin plural for egg cells, the female reproductive cells.

clue.text: Toilet on jetty — even dafter

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet
a pier is a jetty

explanation.surface: A lavatory built on a jetty is sillier still.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopy is informal for crazy, so loopier means crazier still.

clue.text: Elaborates on weight gained by divorcee

indicators.note: gained by says the divorcee comes first and takes on the weight after it

parts.note: a former spouse is an ex
pounds are units of weight

explanation.surface: Someone explains how their ex-partner put on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to explain in detail, which is elaborating on a subject.

clue.text: Give responsibility to reformed nutters

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters of the next word are reshaped

explanation.surface: People who were once crazy have mended their ways and can be given duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' rearranges NUTTERS, British slang for crazy people.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrust is to hand over a duty or responsibility to someone.

clue.text: Times editor did some decorating

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper, so a paper

explanation.surface: An editor at The Times was decorating at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like multiplication or a date, but is The Times, the British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To paper a room is to hang wallpaper, a kind of decorating.

clue.text: Reversible cam?

parts.note: read cam backwards to get mac, a waterproof coat; some such coats can also be worn inside out

explanation.surface: A machine part that can turn either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A mac, short for mackintosh, is a waterproof coat worn in wet weather.

clue.text: Villain shot up in Parisian street

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the street word

parts.note: rue is the French word for street

indicators.note: in a down clue, up turns the word for shot to read bottom to top

parts.note: a shot is a go, an attempt

explanation.surface: A criminal was gunned down in a Paris street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like gunfire, but is a go, turned upward into OG.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or unprincipled person, a rascal.

clue.text: Unprotected skin in long finger

indicators.note: in says the trimmed word goes inside the word for long

parts.note: to pine is to long for something

indicators.note: unprotected strips the outer layer, so the first and last letters go

explanation.surface: Bare skin shows on a long finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' is a verb meaning yearn, not an adjective describing the finger; 'Unprotected' strips skin to KI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinkie is the little finger, the name common in Scotland and North America.

clue.text: Sign in garage vacated by car

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, leaving only the first and last letters

parts.note: the Mini is a British car

explanation.surface: A notice in a garage that a car has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' reads as a notice, but means a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the twins, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Exalted leading role began with new ideas

parts.note: up means leading, as a team two goals up

indicators.note: began picks the first letter, where the word starts
new signals the letters of the next word are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: A star in the lead part started off with fresh ideas and was praised.
explanation.definitionFit: Upraised means raised up or elevated, which is exalted.

clue.text: Old individual, highly valued, got cleared

parts.note: ex means former, so old
one is a single individual
to be rated is to be highly regarded

explanation.surface: A former big shot, once prized, was found not guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exonerated is to be cleared of blame or a charge.

clue.text: Appear ominously close to depression — not good

indicators.note: not good says the letter G, short for good, is taken away

parts.note: gloom is depression or sadness

explanation.surface: Something threatening comes near a state of low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: When something looms it appears large and threatening, often as if near.
